subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Well-to-Wheel Efficiency
description: A quick win: understand Well-to-Wheel Efficiency.

hook.text: Comparing a gas car to an EV isn't fair unless you count all the energy used from source to wheels.

buildup.text: A gas car's chain: drill oil, refine it, truck it, pump it, burn it. Each step loses energy.

discovery.text: An EV's chain: generate electricity, transmit it, charge the battery, drive. Fewer loss points overall.

twist.text: If the electricity comes from coal, an EV's total efficiency advantage shrinks dramatically.

climax.text: On a clean grid, an EV is about 3 times more efficient well-to-wheel than a gas car.

punchline.text: The real comparison starts at the energy source, not the tailpipe.

quiz.question: On a clean grid, how much more efficient is an EV well-to-wheel?
